title: Generating Chip Subsystems Automatically: A New Answer to Manage Chip Design Complexity
gist: Defacto announces SoC subsystem generation with an intent-based Autoconnection capability, claiming HPC subsystems with about a hundred cores and several hundred IPs can be generated in minutes rather than days or weeks. It argues this lowers chip design cost and expertise barriers, and the work is co-funded by the EU's EmpoSoC project.

insights.claim: Modern SoCs combine CPU clusters, accelerators, memories, interconnects and many peripherals from different teams and vendors, and AI, HPC and IoT demand keeps raising the number of blocks and especially connections.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff
insights.so_what: Integration complexity grows faster than block count, pressuring design productivity.

insights.claim: SoC assembly remains painful: connections live in spreadsheets and scripts, every IP must be packaged and checked, and architecture changes force redoing much work, costing days or weeks and requiring specialized skills.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff
insights.so_what: Frames the manual front-end integration step as an automation opportunity.

insights.claim: Design complexity has become a bottleneck for the whole industry.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff
insights.so_what: Supports EDA demand for productivity tools.

insights.claim: Defacto's new solution has designers describe what they want and generates complete subsystems first and then the overall SoC, rather than building connection by connection.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff
insights.so_what: Shifts the design abstraction from netlist wiring to intent.

insights.claim: The flow reads each IP's connectivity, power and timing descriptions, wires blocks per designer intent, restructures the design for smaller, faster, more power-efficient results, and outputs files for downstream verification and implementation.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff
insights.so_what: Describes the end-to-end automated front-end flow.

insights.claim: Autoconnection replaces explicit pin-by-pin connectivity with rules describing intent, from which the tool derives detailed connections as a family of rules, adaptable to any SoC architecture or size.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff
insights.so_what: The core differentiator claimed by Defacto.

insights.claim: The Autoconnection approach can be AI-driven so engineers refine a starting point, but every proposal must be reviewed and approved before any subsystem is generated.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff

insights.claim: The solution supports IP-XACT, power intent and timing constraints, design restructuring, and interoperates with IP configuration tools of the largest IP providers so configured IP flows directly into generation.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff
insights.so_what: Standards and vendor interoperability are needed for adoption in real projects.

insights.claim: Defacto says its solution has been validated by major semiconductor companies on HPC, AI and IoT subsystems.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff
insights.so_what: Claimed validation is unnamed and vendor-reported.

insights.claim: For a typical HPC subsystem with close to a hundred cores and several hundred IPs, generation takes minutes instead of the traditional days or sometimes weeks.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff
insights.so_what: A major claimed productivity gain, unverified independently.
insights.quote: generating a subsystem takes minutes instead of days and sometimes weeks

insights.claim: Faster, cheaper SoC design with less specialist expertise changes chip-design economics, makes more complex chips achievable, and opens the door for emerging players to compete with established semiconductor majors.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff
insights.so_what: If true, lowers entry barriers for challengers and custom silicon.

insights.claim: As chip complexity grows, particularly with AI demands, methods that scale with the design rather than against it will be essential.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff
insights.so_what: Supports demand for automation in EDA.

insights.claim: The innovation is co-funded by the European Union through the EIC Accelerator program under Horizon Europe in a project called EmpoSoC.
insights.speaker: Defacto Staff
insights.so_what: EU public funding supports European EDA startups.
